t: After twelve years of study and organising in the United States and Britain, Nkrumah returned to the Gold Coast in 1947 and built the Convention People's Party, whose landslide in 1951 brought him from prison to the head of government.
He led Ghana to independence in 1957 and made it a centre of Pan-Africanism and the decolonisation of Africa, while spending heavily on roads, harbours, schools and the Akosombo Dam.

His rule grew authoritarian, with detention without trial, a press under state control and, from 1964, a one-party state with himself as president for life, until the military and police overthrew him in 1966.
dyk: While studying at the University of Pennsylvania, Nkrumah worked with the linguist William Everett Welmers, providing the spoken material on which the first descriptive grammar of his native Fante dialect of the Akan language was based.
ev: Kwame Nkrumah is born at Nkroful in the Gold Coast
He founds the Convention People's Party
The party wins the Gold Coast election in a landslide and he is released from prison to form a government
The Gold Coast becomes independent as Ghana, with Nkrumah as prime minister
Ghana becomes a republic and Nkrumah is elected its president
A constitutional amendment makes Ghana a one-party state with Nkrumah as president for life
He is overthrown in a coup while on a state visit to China
Nkrumah dies in Bucharest, after years of exile in Guinea

f.born: 21 September 1909 by his own account (his mother later gave 1912), at Nkroful in the Nzema area of the Gold Coast; son of a goldsmith, Opanyin Kofi Nwiana Ngolomah, of the Asona clan, and Elizabeth Nyanibah, a fishmonger and petty trader
f.died: 27 April 1972, in Bucharest, of an unknown but apparently incurable sickness, after six years of exile in Conakry, Guinea
f.role: General secretary of the United Gold Coast Convention (1947); founder and leader of the Convention People's Party (1949); Leader of Government Business (1951) and Prime Minister of the Gold Coast (1952-1957); Prime Minister of Ghana (1957-1960); President of Ghana (1960-1966), from 1964 president for life of a one-party state
f.known: Leading Ghana to independence in 1957; the Convention People's Party and Positive Action; Pan-Africanism and the founding of the Organisation of African Unity; the Volta River Project and the Akosombo Dam; expansion of schooling; the Preventive Detention Act and the one-party state; the 1966 coup
